name: MS-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+11 district with long-serving incumbent Bennie Thompson
Thompson's cash advantage of roughly $1.36 million to $38,000
Prediction markets price Thompson near 97 percent
No public polling, but no spending or fundraising signs of a contest
model.rationale: The district's D+11 lean, Thompson's long incumbency, and his overwhelming financial edge over Ron Eller all point the same direction, and prediction markets price Thompson near 97 percent. With no polling or outside spending suggesting a race, this stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late outside spending against Thompson or polling showing Eller within single digits would warrant revisiting, but no such signs have emerged.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bennie Thompson has represented Mississippi's second district for decades, and the seat's D+11 partisan lean gives Republicans a steep climb. Thompson enters the general election with about $1.36 million on hand after raising more than $928,000, while Republican Ron Eller has raised roughly $64,000 and holds just under $38,000. No outside groups have spent in the race, and an independent candidate draws minimal resources.

With no public polling available, the outlook rests on fundamentals: the district's lean, Thompson's incumbency, and his lopsided financial advantage. Prediction markets price Thompson's chances near 97 percent, and his recent reelection margins have been wide. Nothing in the fundraising or spending picture signals a competitive contest, so the forecast places Thompson comfortably ahead, with uncertainty driven mainly by the absence of polling rather than any evidence of a race.
